html:
James Cook was killed at Kealakekua Bay on the island of Hawaiʻi on 14 February 1779, in a fight with Hawaiians over a stolen boat.

Cook had arrived during the Makahiki season and was treated with great honour. When his ships came back for repairs, relations broke down, and he was struck down on the shore while trying to take a chief hostage.

News of his voyages put Hawaii on the charts. Within a few decades traders came for sandalwood and supplies, and the young chief Kamehameha, who had met Cook's ships, used Western guns to unite the islands into the Kingdom of Hawaii.
sum: James Cook was killed at Kealakekua Bay on the island of Hawaiʻi on 14 February 1779, in a fight with Hawaiians over a stolen boat.
